_readme: 12 worked events in the living-world schema (16 objects: the car call and the journalist each have a follow-up event, and the boots chain is 3 linked events). Money is in WEEKS of your own weekly income (moneyWeeks), so one event reads right in the National League and the Premier League. boss/team/fans/fame/reputation are the game's existing bars (DilemmaEffect keys). npc deltas move ONE person's respect / bond / grudge (0-100). remember writes one line into that person's memory. All names of people are filled from the cast at fire time; brands are invented.

events.title: The legend at training
setup: You walk out and the whole squad is stood in a circle. {legend.name} is in the middle in an old club tracksuit, doing keepy-ups.
{mate.short}: "He's been asking which one is {you.short}."
{legend.short}: "You're the one they sing about now? First to three. Me and you. In front of this lot."

outcomes.text: 3-{score.them}. The squad goes mad. He takes his boots off and hands them to you. "Look after them."
He nutmegs you for the third. The lads are howling. He ruffles your hair. "Come and find me when you're ready."

choices.label: "Make it interesting. My car against your boots."

outcomes.text: He laughs all the way through losing. Boots, and a signed shirt for the house.
He holds his hand out for the keys. He means it. {mate.short} gives you a lift home.
The circle breaks up. A few of the lads look at their boots.

callbacks.line: "Nice motor, by the way. Does about twelve to the gallon."
"Still hiding from old men, are we?"

needs: cutscene story 'legend-challenge' (training-ground, circle of mates, mentor role)
build.phone: text version: the same choices, the 1v1 as the existing relationship game (RelationshipGame)

events.title: "Can I borrow the motor?"
setup: Your phone lights up on the dash: {mate.name}.
{mate.short}: "Mate. Big favour. It's my mum's sixtieth Saturday night. Can I turn up in yours? I'll have it back Sunday, washed."

outcomes.text: It comes back Sunday, washed, with a full tank and a box of your favourite KIB cans on the seat.
Sunday night. A photo arrives first. The front wing is against a bollard. "I am so, so sorry."
"Yeah. No. Fair enough." He hangs up a bit quick.

choices.label: "I'll do better. I'll drive you there myself."

outcomes.text: You drop him at the door. His mum comes out and makes you stay for cake. There is a photo of you two on her fridge now.

callbacks.line: (post-match) "Thought about squaring it. Then I thought about that car."
callbacks.effect: In a tight chance he shoots instead of squaring it 10% more often while grudge>=20

callbacks.line: "Mum still asks after you."

build.phone: same call on the 3D phone, no driving

events.title: He wants to make it right
setup: {mate.short} is waiting by your table with an envelope.
"That's the repair. All of it. And I've told the gaffer it was me, before the papers make it you."

outcomes.text: Square. He looks relieved.
He does not know what to say. He will not forget it.

callbacks.line: He is the first to stand up for you in the dressing room (team loss halved).

events.title: "Don't say anything. Just listen."
setup: {agent.name}: "Don't say anything. Just listen. {club.short} had a man at the last three. They'll come in the summer. I can let that be known, or I can keep it very quiet. Your call."

outcomes.text: By Thursday it is on every feed. Your club offers new terms within a fortnight. The gaffer does not look at you in training.

choices.label: "Keep it quiet. I've a season to finish."

outcomes.text: "Your funeral." He means it kindly. Mostly.

choices.label: Hang up. Go and tell the gaffer yourself.

outcomes.text: He listens, nods once. "Nobody has ever told me first." The armband talk comes a month later.

callbacks.line: "You like the papers. Read about the team in them on Saturday."
His opening ask for you is 5% lower: "I work as hard as I'm trusted."

needs: agent as a persistent person (not in the game yet: STAR_ROADMAP item 18)

events.title: The man from the tabloid
setup: {hack.name} of the {hack.outlet} steps across you in the mixed zone, phone up, recording.
"{you.short}. Two shots, none on target. Are you worth the money?"

choices.label: "Not today I wasn't. That's on me."

outcomes.text: He lowers the phone a little. The piece runs under 'NO EXCUSES'. Fair.
"Nothing to say, then." He says it loudly, for the others.

choices.label: "Have you ever kicked a ball in your life?"

outcomes.text: The clip has two million views by breakfast. Your own fans love it. He does not.

callbacks.line: His match reports mark you 0.5 kinder for 10 weeks.
He gets the story first, and the fame/fans hit is 1.5x.

needs: 3 named journalists as persistent people tied to media accounts (broadsheet, tabloid, insider archetypes already exist)

events.title: "Sources close to the dressing room"
setup: Your phone will not stop. {hack.outlet}: "{you.short} 'THINKS HE'S BIGGER THAN THE CLUB', say team-mates."
{if source}The quotes sound a lot like {source.short}.{/if}

outcomes.text: It burns for a week and goes out.

choices.label: Ring him. Offer the sit-down interview he wanted.

outcomes.text: An hour in a hotel bar. The follow-up piece is called 'The other side of {you.short}'.
You put the paper on {source.short}'s seat in the canteen. He does not deny it. The room goes quiet.

callbacks.line: He becomes your dressing-room rival (see rvl-new-signing-shirt).

events.title: The lad on his own
setup: {kid.name}, {kid.age}, up from the academy this week, is eating on his own with his headphones in.
{mate.short} waves you over to the usual table.

outcomes.text: He takes one headphone out. Ten minutes later he is telling you about his nan's jollof. He watches where you sit every day after that.

choices.label: Shout him over to the lads' table.

outcomes.text: He comes. The lads rip his trainers apart for ten minutes. He is grinning by the end.
He pretends not to hear, goes red, and leaves his food.
Nobody notices. That is rather the point.

callbacks.line: He runs the length of the pitch to you. Post-match: "First day. He sat with me. I don't forget that." (fans +3)
Event 'fdh-the-kid-is-the-star-now' unlocks: he asks YOU to stay another year.

events.title: A day at the races
setup: You and {mate.short} in the owners' bar. He has a tip from his cousin: number 7, 'Offside Trap', 12 to 1 in the fourth.
{if you.horse}Your own {you.horse.name} runs in the fifth.{/if}

choices.label: Put a proper bet on his tip.

outcomes.text: It wins by a nose. He is on the table. You are both on the back pages, grinning.
Fifth of nine. He cannot look at you. "My cousin is dead to me."

choices.label: A fiver each way, for a laugh.

outcomes.text: A good day. Nothing happens, in the best way. He tells you he is thinking of leaving in the summer; you are the first to know.

choices.label: "Forget his cousin. Back mine in the fifth."

outcomes.text: {you.horse.name} by two lengths. {mate.short} had fifty on it.
Last. "Lovely looking animal, though," he says, tearing up his slip.

callbacks.line: "How's the donkey?"
If he is sold: a goodbye text that names the day. If you ask the boss to keep him (boss respect>=60) he stays.

build.phone: still + choices; horse race uses the existing race

events.title: He wants your number
setup: {rival.name}, the new {rival.fee} signing, is stood at your peg holding the number {you.number} shirt.
"I've worn this since I was nine. The club said to ask you. So I'm asking." {kitman.short} is pretending to fold socks.

outcomes.text: He hangs it back up, slowly. "Okay. We'll see who's wearing it in May."

choices.label: Hand it over. "Numbers don't score goals."

outcomes.text: He did not expect that. The kit man raises an eyebrow. You pick a new number tomorrow.
Bar, first go. He shakes your hand properly.
He hits it. You don't. A deal is a deal.

callbacks.line: Event 'rvl-may-reckoning': whoever scored more. If you: "Keep the shirt. You earned it." (grudge to respect). If him: he asks again, in front of everyone.
He points at his own number, at you, on the bench.

needs: duel tracker (his goals v yours on the Home screen)

events.title: Dad's old club
setup: Dad rings. He never rings. "The Sunday side. The one I took you to when you were five. The council want four grand for the pitch or they fold. I'm not asking. I'm just telling you."

choices.label: Pay it. Today. Say nothing publicly.

outcomes.text: He goes quiet for a long time. "Your mum would have liked that." They paint your name on the hut.

choices.label: Pay it, and bring the cameras.

outcomes.text: Lovely pictures. Dad stands at the back of every one.
"No. No, course." The club folds in the spring. He tells you in passing.

callbacks.line: The Sunday side's kids form the guard of honour.
"I'd ask, but I know how you are with money."

needs: family as persistent people (dad, mum, sibling: not in the game yet)

events.title: The wrong boots
setup: {mate.short} chucks you a prototype pair from his brand, Vanta. "Try them. One session. Nobody's watching." They feel unbelievable.
Somebody was watching. A photo is on a fan account by tea time. {rep.name} from {you.bootBrand} texts: "Tell me that's edited."

outcomes.text: "It had better not." A fine comes off the next payment.

choices.label: "They're better than yours. Match them or I walk."

outcomes.text: A day of silence. Then a new offer: fee up, and your own colourway.
"Then walk." The deal ends on Friday. Vanta do not ring.
They believe you. His brand does not see the funny side, and neither does he when he finds out why.

callbacks.line: No boot offers from that brand for 2 seasons.
"Ask one of your sponsors." He turns down the next two social actions.

events.title: 2:14 a.m.
setup: A text from a number you do not know. A photo: you, at the roulette table, clock on the wall behind you. 2:14 a.m. Match in {daysToMatch} days.
"Nice night? {hack.outlet} would pay me 5k for this. You can pay me 10."

outcomes.text: The photo never appears.
He takes the money and sells it anyway. Now there are two stories.

choices.label: Go to the gaffer before it breaks.

outcomes.text: He is furious for four minutes and useful for ten. You are on the bench Saturday. The club puts out a line before the paper does.

choices.label: "Sell it. I was there. So what."

outcomes.text: Front page Friday. Two goals Saturday. Sunday's headline: 'WHAT A GAMBLE'.
Front page Friday. A stinker Saturday. They boo you off.

callbacks.line: A text from the gaffer as you walk in: "Don't."
The next blackmailer asks double: "I hear you pay."

needs: works with lib/star/casinoScandal.ts (already in the game): one of the two may fire per visit, not both

events.title: It's probably nothing
setup: Your hamstring tightens in the warm-up. {physio.name} presses a thumb into it and watches your face.
"It's a 2 out of 10. Play Saturday and it's fine, or it's a 7. Sit out and it's definitely fine. {boss.short} will ask me. What do I tell him?"

choices.label: "Tell him the truth. I'll sit this one out."

outcomes.text: You watch from the stand. Monday it feels brand new.
It holds. Just.
Sixty-third minute. You know before you hit the ground.

choices.label: "Bench. Twenty minutes if we need it."

outcomes.text: She nods. "That I can sell."

callbacks.line: She gets you back 1 week sooner: "You do the rehab. Most don't."
The 'tell him I'm fine' choice is gone. "Not again. I'm telling him."

needs: physio as a persistent staff person

events.title: Chain 1 of 3: "Size nine?"
setup: Forty minutes to kick-off. {kid.name}'s sole has come clean off. He has one pair. He is trying to tape it and his hands are shaking.
He sees you looking. "You're a nine, aren't you?"

outcomes.text: He plays the game of his life in them.

choices.label: "Tape's in the physio bag. Sort yourself out."

outcomes.text: He plays in a taped boot and comes off at half time with a blister the size of a coin.

events.title: Chain 2 of 3: He tries to give them back
setup: {kid.short} is waiting with your boots, cleaned better than you have ever cleaned them. "I get paid Friday. I'll get my own."

outcomes.text: He holds them like they might break.

choices.label: Sign them first. "For when you're famous."

outcomes.text: "When, not if?" "When."
Fair is fair.

events.title: Chain 3 of 3: Years later
setup: The tunnel. {kid.name} is {kid.age} now, captain of {kid.club}{if kid.club==you.club}, your captain{/if}. He is stood next to you in the line.
{if mem:you-signed-the-boots-when-not-if}He lifts one foot. Your old boots. Your signature, nearly worn off. "When, not if. You said."{/if}
{if mem:you-gave-him-the-boots}"I've still got them. They're in a glass case at my mum's."{/if}
{if mem:you-told-him-to-tape-it}He does not look at you. "Tape's in the physio bag," he says, to nobody.{/if}

outcomes.text: After the match he tells the cameras the story. It is the most shared clip of the season.
He hugs you before the handshake line. The cameras catch it.
He marks you all game like it is personal. It is. He scores and runs to the away end past you.

needs: uses the existing 'walkout' story + a 'stare-down' or new 'old-friend' beat; kid's world ageing already exists (worldAgeing.ts)
build.phone: the same cut scene (tunnel is already phone-framed)
